title: Algebraization of proper flat formal curves over a power-series ring
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], put $R=k[[t]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and $R_n=R/(t^n)=k[t]/(t^n)$ for $n\geq1$. Suppose $X_n\to\operatorname{Spec}R_n$ are proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented schemes [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], equipped with compatible identifications $X_{n+1}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R_{n+1}}\operatorname{Spec}R_n\cong X_n$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and $\dim X_1\leq1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then there is a flat finitely presented morphism $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, projective in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective], with compatible $R_n$-isomorphisms $Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}R_n\cong X_n$ for all $n\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 0E7R, lemma-formal-algebraic-space-proper-reldim-1, with the properness hypothesis used in its proof made explicit; flatness follows from more-morphisms.tex, Tag 0D4G, lemma-check-flatness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds, on the special fibre and from flatness over the field k((t)) on the generic fibre; finite presentation follows over the Noetherian base.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] with coefficient field $k$ and one variable. Thus $R=k[[t]]$ is a Noetherian complete local domain with maximal ideal $(t)$ and residue field $k$. Each $R_n$ is Noetherian: an ascending chain of ideals in $R_n$ lifts to a chain of ideals of $R$ containing $(t^n)$, so it stabilizes. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R_n$ are Noetherian schemes (the one affine chart has Noetherian coordinate ring). Every $X_n$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since its proper structure morphism is of finite type.

The specified cartesian identifications define $i_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal], this is the closed immersion cut out by $t^n\mathcal O_{X_{n+1}}$. This ideal is nilpotent, since $t^{n+1}=0$ on $X_{n+1}$. On each affine chart all prime ideals contain a nilpotent ideal; the prime-ideal correspondence for a quotient therefore identifies all closed sets on the two spectra. Hence $i_n$ is a homeomorphism, and all $X_n$ have the same topological dimension as $X_1$, at most one. Their underlying topological spaces are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal].

source.place: Tag 0E7R, lemma-formal-algebraic-space-proper-reldim-1, second paragraph; quotient geometry as in morphisms.tex Tag 01R5

proof.text: The proper $k$-scheme $X_1$ is separated and finite type, so [lem-sc-dim-one-ample-invertible] supplies an ample invertible module $L_1$; its statement includes the empty and zero-dimensional cases. Inductively suppose $L_n$ has been chosen. Apply [lem-sc-pic-lift-closed-immersion-dim-le-one] to $i_n:X_n\hookrightarrow X_{n+1}$. Its ambient scheme has Noetherian underlying space and dimension at most one by step 2. We obtain an invertible $L_{n+1}$ and an isomorphism $\varphi_n:i_n^*L_{n+1}\cong L_n$. Starting at $n=1$, recursive choice gives the whole sequence. For $m<n$ define the comparison by composing the adjacent $\varphi_j$ using the pullback composition isomorphisms of [def-pc-module-pullback]; these composites satisfy the cocycle law by associativity. No assertion that each lift is canonically determined is needed.

source.place: Tag 0E7R, first two paragraphs; varieties.tex Tags 0A25/09NZ and 09NY

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-polarized-formal-algebraization] to $A=R$, $I=(t)$ and the system $(X_n,L_n,\varphi_n)$. Completeness and Noetherianity hold by step 1, the cartesian condition is the given one, $X_1$ is proper by hypothesis, and $L_1$ is ample by step 3. It gives a proper $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, a closed immersion into some finite $\mathbf P^N_R$, and all the required compatible isomorphisms $Y\times_RR_n\cong X_n$, which the cited statement gives over $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}R_n$, i.e. as $R_n$-isomorphisms; step 6 uses this to transport the flatness of $X_n\to\operatorname{Spec}R_n$. This supplies the projectivity convention in the statement, including compatibility at every stage.

source.place: Tag 089A, theorem-algebraization, including the finite projective-space construction in the proof

proof.text: The proper morphism $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is of finite type, hence quasi-compact, and separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; it is quasi-separated because its diagonal is a closed immersion, and a closed immersion is affine, hence quasi-compact. Its target is locally Noetherian by step 1, so [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes it locally of finite presentation. Together with quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness this is finite presentation, as defined in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Also $Y$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian].

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; finite-presentation convention and Noetherian finite-type criterion

proof.text: Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be any affine open of $Y$. The ring $B$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. For every $n$, [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal] identifies $U\times_RR_n$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B/t^nB)$. Under the isomorphism of step 4 this is an open subscheme of $X_n$. Its morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}R_n$ is flat: restriction to an open does not change the local rings in [def-weil-flat-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine], $B/t^nB$ is a flat $R_n$-module for every $n\geq1$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-powers] to the ring map $R\to B$, ideal $(t)$, and $B$-module $M=B$. Both rings are Noetherian and $M$ is generated by $1$; the required flatness of every quotient is step 6. For every prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ containing $t$, the conclusion is that $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] this is the local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ at the corresponding point of $U$. Its image in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is $(t)$, where the base local ring is $R$ itself because $R$ is local. Thus $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is flat at every point of its closed fibre, by [def-weil-flat-morphism].

For completeness there are no other base points except the generic point: a nonzero power series is $t^r u$ for its least nonzero exponent $r$, where $u$ has nonzero constant coefficient and is a unit by [lem-weil-power-series-unit-constant-coefficient]. A nonzero proper prime ideal therefore contains $t$ and equals $(t)$. At the remaining prime $(0)$, the base local ring is the fraction field of the domain $R$, by the localization description in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. For a point $y$ above it, $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is a module over that field, hence flat by the field-module assertion in [lem-pc-flat-field]. Step 7 treats every point above $(t)$, and these two cases exhaust $Y$. The local-ring definition [def-weil-flat-morphism] proves global flatness. Together with steps 4 and 5 this proves all clauses.
